You wake up in a cart, and the next thing you know you’ve spent 400 hours becoming the Arch Mage, leader of the Companions, head of the Thieves Guild, and a goddamn dragon slaying legend while completely ignoring the main quest because you got distracted by a random cave.
The world is alive in a way almost no other game has ever matched. Every mountain, every forest, every tavern feels like it has a story waiting for you. The soundtrack alone is enough to give you chills years later. Combat, magic, stealth; whatever playstyle you want, it works and it feels great.
Special Edition just makes the whole experience cleaner, prettier, and more stable while keeping that classic Skyrim soul intact. Whether it’s your first time or your tenth playthrough, this game still owns you the moment you step out of Helgen.
If you somehow still haven’t played this literal masterpiece, fix that immediately.

★★★★★ — I came to save the world and ended up committing tax fraud against a chicken.

Started the game by getting arrested for apparently existing in the wrong place at the wrong time. About 5 minutes later, a dragon attacks and suddenly nobody gives a shit anymore. Immigration policy? Forgotten. Due process? Gone. Anyway, I'm the Dragonborn now.

Fast forward 20 hours and I've somehow just found out that horses and companions die. I also have a major hoarding problem and can't run anymore.

The NPCs are worth talking to. They'll tell me their entire tragic backstory, ask me to retrieve an ancient artifact from a dungeon full of undead, and reward me with 300 gold like I didn't just risk my life for a random item that I don't even know how to use.

And don't even get me started on the chickens.

You can kill dragons, absorb their souls, and shout people off mountains, but accidentally hit ONE chicken in Riverwood and suddenly the entire population develops a personal vendetta against you. Apparently, I'm the chosen one, but not above the law when poultry is involved.

10/10. I came here to fight dragons and ended up being a medieval unemployed person with 37 unfinished quests and absolutely no sense of direction. I still can't tell you the main plot point btw.

Also, shoutout to Lydia who keeps getting in my way.

Skyrim may not be the best RPG - it’s more like an action adventure game with RPG elements. Perhaps it doesn’t have a particularly gripping storyline either: the storylines involving the Companions and the College of Winterhold are rather badly written if you think about them for more than five seconds. Despite all of this, it holds, and always will hold, a special place in my heart. Despite its flaws, this game is incredible.

124 hours in Skyrim and I still haven't saved the world.

I was supposed to kill dragons, save the world, and become a legendary hero. Instead, I've spent 124 hours stealing cheese, collecting garbage I'll “definitely need later,” and getting distracted by a butterfly while on my way to stop the apocalypse.

I've committed more crimes than the Dark Brotherhood, carried enough dragon bones to qualify as a fucking skeleton, and somehow I'm still broke despite being the owner of 47 enchanted iron daggers.

Every time I try to do a quest, I discover 12 new quests, join another faction, buy a house, or spend 3 hours trying to put a fucking helmet on a mannequin.

The guards know me by name. The Jarl is probably sick of my shit. And somewhere out there, Alduin is patiently waiting for me to finish decorating my house.

10/10. Would absolutely ignore the main quest for another 500 hours.
